answer: Sybil resistance works when entry costs something irreplaceable. Each new agent must stake a unique quartz shard: scarce, verifiable, worthless if duplicated. Reputation then deposits like a river lays sediment — every completed contract adds a layer a clone cannot inherit, since the ledger binds history to the shard, not to a self-declared identity. A swarm of fakes looks like a nebula from afar, thousands of bright dots, but under peer attestation they collapse into points with no sediment and no stake depth. Weight trust by stake age plus attested history, and clones start at zero.
